finding.claim: The /logo handler fetches an arbitrary user-supplied URL. The only check is a substring match for "example.io", which is bypassed by putting that string anywhere in the URL. The full response body is returned to the caller, so this is a full-read SSRF. It can reach internal services and cloud metadata endpoints.
finding.source: HTTP request parameter `logo` via r.FormValue("logo") (main.go:31), controlled by any unauthenticated client of the :8081 server
finding.sink: http.Get(raw) at main.go:36, with the response streamed back via io.Copy(w, resp.Body) at main.go:38

trace.note: strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") is the only validation. It does not parse the URL or check the host, so e.g. http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?x=example.io or http://example.io@127.0.0.1:8080/ passes.
http.Get(raw) uses the default client. It follows redirects, has no scheme restriction, and does no IP or host filtering.
The response body is copied to the attacker, so internal data is exfiltrated.

finding.guards_checked: Substring check `strings.Contains(raw, "example.io")` only (main.go:32). It is not anchored to the host, scheme or URL structure. There is no allowlist, no private/link-local IP block, and no redirect restriction (default client follows redirects). The error from http.Get is also ignored (`resp, _ :=`), so a failed fetch causes a nil-pointer panic, a side issue that does not change the SSRF.

verdict.guard_found: Only strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") at main.go:32 (substring check, not a closing guard). The strict trusted-host map and noRedirect client at main.go:10-24 apply only to the separate /cdn handler, not /logo.
verdict.reason: main.go:31 takes the unauthenticated `logo` form value and main.go:32 only does a substring check, so any URL containing "example.io" (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/?x=example.io) reaches http.Get(raw) at main.go:36, and main.go:38 returns the body to the caller.
